target: Paid â rhoi'r gorau iddi, mae'r arholiad bron ar ben.
english: Don't give up, the exam is nearly over.
tip: 'paid â' tells one person not to do something: 'paid â rhoi'r gorau' means don't give up.

target: Buon ni yng Nghaerdydd.
english: We were in Cardiff.
tip: 'buon ni' means we were, the plain past of 'bod' (to be); the '-on ni' ending is the we part.

target: Canodd hi yn yr eisteddfod y llynedd.
english: She sang at the eisteddfod last year.
tip: The ending '-odd' marks a past he or she: 'canu' becomes 'canodd hi' (she sang).

target: Mae cennin Pedr ym mhobman yn y gwanwyn.
english: There are daffodils everywhere in spring.
tip: Before an m sound, 'yn' (in) becomes 'ym': 'pobman' turns into 'ym mhobman', 'p' mutating to 'mh'.

target: Mae gen i brofiad o weithio gyda thimau.
english: I have experience of working with teams.
tip: Welsh has no verb for have: 'mae gen i brofiad' is literally there is with me experience, meaning I have experience.

target: Dw i'n byw yng Nghaerdydd ers pum mlynedd.
english: I live in Cardiff and have been there for five years.
tip: After 'pum' (five), 'blynedd' becomes 'mlynedd': 'pum mlynedd'. Some numbers nasal-mutate the following noun.

target: Mae'r cigydd yn torri'r cig gyda chyllell finiog.
english: The butcher cuts the meat with a sharp knife.
tip: An adjective softens after a feminine noun: 'miniog' becomes 'finiog' in 'cyllell finiog' (sharp knife).

target: Mae hi wedi byw yng Nghaerdydd ers deng mlynedd.
english: She has lived in Cardiff for ten years.
tip: 'ers' marks time still ongoing: 'ers deng mlynedd' means for ten years and counting, up to now.

target: Dyma'r afon hiraf yng Nghymru.
english: This is the longest river in Wales.
tip: The ending '-af' makes the most: 'hir' (long) becomes 'hiraf' (longest) in 'yr afon hiraf'.

target: Dyma'r traeth harddaf yng Nghymru.
english: This is the most beautiful beach in Wales.
tip: 'dyma' means here is or this is, pointing at what is in front of you: 'dyma'r traeth', this is the beach.

target: Mae hiraeth dwfn arna i am fy mro enedigol.
english: I have a deep longing for my native land.
tip: Feelings sit on you: 'mae hiraeth dwfn arna i' means I feel a deep longing, where 'arna i' is 'ar' (on) plus me.

target: Chwe chant o bunnoedd.
english: Six hundred pounds.
tip: 'chwe' (six) triggers aspirate mutation, so 'cant' becomes 'chant', as in 'chwe chant' (six hundred).

target: Sawl plentyn sydd gennych chi?
english: How many children do you have?
tip: 'sawl' (how many) always takes a singular noun, so it is 'sawl plentyn' (how many children), never a plural.

target: Gyda phob parch, dw i'n anghytuno.
english: With all respect, I disagree.
tip: 'gyda' triggers aspirate mutation, so 'pob' becomes 'phob' in 'gyda phob parch' (with all respect).

target: Mae pob ymdrech fach yn gwneud gwahaniaeth.
english: Every small effort makes a difference.
tip: 'ymdrech' is feminine, so a following adjective soft-mutates: 'bach' becomes 'fach' in 'ymdrech fach' (small effort).

target: Mae'r maes parcio yn llawn ar ddydd Sadwrn.
english: The car park is full on Saturday.
tip: 'ar' triggers soft mutation, so 'dydd' becomes 'ddydd': 'ar ddydd Sadwrn' (on Saturday).

target: Bydd y tywydd yn heulog y prynhawn yma.
english: The weather will be sunny this afternoon.
tip: 'bydd' is the future of 'bod' (to be): 'bydd y tywydd yn heulog' means the weather will be sunny.

target: Paid ag anghofio cau'r drws ar dy ôl.
english: Don't forget to close the door behind you.
tip: 'paid â' plus a verb is the singular way to say don't: 'paid ag anghofio' (don't forget).

target: Os gorffenni di'n gynnar, tyrd i ymuno â ni.
english: If you finish early, come and join us.
tip: The linking 'yn' softens a following adjective, so 'cynnar' becomes 'gynnar': 'di'n gynnar' (you finish early).

target: Hyd y gwn i, mae siop y pentref yn dal ar agor ar foreau Sadwrn.
english: As far as I know, the village shop is still open on Saturday mornings.
tip: 'hyd y gwn i' is a set phrase for as far as I know; 'gwn' is I know, from 'gwybod'.

target: Mae'r ddadl am annibyniaeth yn parhau.
english: The debate about independence continues.
tip: 'dadl' is feminine, so it soft-mutates after the article: 'mae'r ddadl' (the debate).

target: Mae gan Eluned gi bach o'r enw Pero.
english: Eluned has a little dog called Pero.
tip: Possession uses 'mae gan', and the thing owned soft-mutates: 'ci' becomes 'gi' in 'mae gan Eluned gi' (Eluned has a dog).

target: Prynodd Rhodri bapur newydd a llaeth ar y ffordd.
english: Rhodri bought a newspaper and milk on the way.
tip: The object of a short-form verb soft-mutates, so 'papur' becomes 'bapur': 'prynodd Rhodri bapur' (Rhodri bought a paper).

target: Dathlodd hi ei phen-blwydd yn dri deg yr wythnos diwethaf.
english: She celebrated her birthday when she turned thirty last week.
tip: 'ei' (her) triggers aspirate mutation, so 'pen-blwydd' becomes 'phen-blwydd': 'ei phen-blwydd' (her birthday).

target: Mae caws Cymru cystal ag unrhyw gaws yn y byd.
english: Welsh cheese is as good as any in the world.
tip: 'cystal' is the as-good-as form of 'da' (good), meaning as good as: 'cystal ag unrhyw gaws' (as good as any cheese).

target: Roedd hi wedi ymarfer y gân am wythnosau cyn yr Eisteddfod.
english: She had practised the song for weeks before the Eisteddfod.
tip: 'roedd' plus 'wedi' makes the had-done past: 'roedd hi wedi ymarfer' means she had practised.

target: Adeiladodd Angharad wal gerrig o gwmpas y cae fel na fyddai'r defaid yn dianc.
english: Angharad built a stone wall around the field so that the sheep would not escape.
tip: 'fel na' plus 'fyddai' means so that ... would not: 'fel na fyddai'r defaid yn dianc' (so the sheep would not escape).

target: Mae Cymru'n anelu at fod yn garbon niwtral erbyn 2050.
english: Wales aims to be carbon neutral by 2050.
tip: 'erbyn' marks a deadline, meaning by a point in time: 'erbyn 2050' (by 2050).

target: Sefwch ar eich traed!
english: Stand up!
tip: The '-wch' ending makes a command plural or polite: 'sefwch' means stand to a group or formally.

target: Mae gen i anifail anwes.
english: I have a pet.
tip: Welsh has no verb have: 'mae gen i' means I have, literally there is with me: 'mae gen i anifail anwes'.
